subject.title: [Feature]: Add native checkpoint engine with deterministic resume and diff

question: Should OpenClaw own a general native checkpoint/replay contract, and which first product boundary should it support: explicit session snapshots, restart recovery, or structured task-boundary continuation?
rationale: The choice determines protocol surface, durable-state ownership, replay safety, UI/CLI semantics, and how several overlapping open issues should be consolidated; source inspection cannot select that permanent boundary safely.

options.title: Design one core contract
options.body: Sponsor a versioned checkpoint protocol and SQLite-backed state model that supports the three use cases incrementally without separate competing engines.

options.title: Start with session snapshots
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13700 the first scoped implementation and defer deterministic task replay and restart automation.

options.title: Keep recovery narrowly scoped
options.body: Retain compaction and restart recovery primitives but decline a general user-visible checkpoint/replay engine.

recommendation.title: Design one core contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a versioned checkpoint protocol and SQLite-backed state model that supports the three use cases incrementally without separate competing engines.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available owner signal from the current compaction checkpoint implementation and the issue's explicit product follow-up discussion.
